This vignette describes how to add an adult mosquito (**MY**) model module to
[`ramp.library`](https://github.com/dd-harp/ramp.library). Before creating a
new module, check whether the model family is already available in the
SimBA library. For an overview of the component interfaces, see the
[`ramp.xds` MY interface vignette](https://dd-harp.github.io/ramp.xds/articles/MY-interface.html).

An MY module represents adult mosquito ecology and, when applicable, pathogen
infection dynamics in mosquitoes. It supplies methods that integrate with
[`ramp.xds`](https://github.com/dd-harp/ramp.xds), which provides the shared
model setup, transmission, egg-laying, and solver interfaces.

## Create a module template

This vignette's R code chunks can be extracted to create a starting R file.
Download `MY-How_To_Add_Model.Rmd`, set your working directory to the folder
containing it, then run:

```{r, eval=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
knitr::purl(
  "MY-How_To_Add_Model.Rmd",
  output = "adult-MY-newMYname.R",
  documentation = 0,
  quiet = TRUE
)
```

Replace `newMYname` throughout the extracted file with a short, unique class
name for the model. Review every placeholder and adapt the methods to the
model's equations and state variables before using the file.

## Conventions

- MY methods dispatch on the class of `xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]`; use `s` as the
  vector-species index in method signatures and calls.
- Use `get_MY_vars(y, xds_obj, s)` to retrieve named state variables, and keep
  the order of variables consistent across `setup_MY_ix`, `get_MY_vars`,
  initial values, and the dynamics.
- Document the model's state variables, parameters, equations, assumptions,
  and relevant references in roxygen.
- Add tests for setup, parameter and initial-value changes, dynamics, and any
  model-specific outputs.

## Model object and state variables

`make_MY_obj_newMYname` creates the module-specific list and assigns its class.
`setup_MY_obj.newMYname` attaches it to the full `xds_obj`. Include the
parameters and any model-specific objects needed by the equations. Parameters
that use the shared bionomics or dispersal interfaces should be set up with
the corresponding `ramp.xds` helpers.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Make the model object for newMYname
#' @param nPatches number of patches
#' @param options named values that override defaults
#' @return a list
#' @export
make_MY_obj_newMYname <- function(nPatches, options = list(), p1 = 1) {
  with(options, {
    MY_obj <- list()
    MY_obj$p1 <- checkIt(p1, nPatches)
    MY_obj$nPatches <- nPatches
    class(MY_obj) <- "newMYname"
    MY_obj
  })
}

#' @title Set up the newMYname MY module
#' @description Implements [ramp.xds::setup_MY_obj] for newMYname.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::setup_MY_obj
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @export
setup_MY_obj.newMYname <- function(MYname, xds_obj, options = list(), s = 1) {
  xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]] <- make_MY_obj_newMYname(xds_obj$nPatches, options)
  xds_obj <- setup_MY_inits(xds_obj, options = options, s = s)
  xds_obj
}
```

### State-variable indices

`setup_MY_ix.newMYname` assigns a contiguous index range to each state
variable. The example follows the SI implementation; add or remove index
ranges to match the model and store them in the named list at
`xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]$ix`.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Set up indices for newMYname
#' @description Implements [ramp.xds::setup_MY_ix] for newMYname.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::setup_MY_ix
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @importFrom utils tail
#' @export
setup_MY_ix.newMYname <- function(xds_obj, s) {
  with(xds_obj, {
    M_ix <- seq(from = max_ix + 1, length.out = nPatches)
    max_ix <- tail(M_ix, 1)

    Y_ix <- seq(from = max_ix + 1, length.out = nPatches)
    max_ix <- tail(Y_ix, 1)

    xds_obj$max_ix <- max_ix
    xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]$ix <- list(M_ix = M_ix, Y_ix = Y_ix)
    xds_obj
  })
}
```

`get_MY_vars.newMYname` maps the dependent-variable vector `y` to the named
state variables used in the equations. Include only variables that belong to
the module's state vector; do not add host variables unless they are actual MY
states.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Get newMYname state variables
#' @description Implements [ramp.xds::get_MY_vars] for newMYname.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::get_MY_vars
#' @return a named list
#' @export
get_MY_vars.newMYname <- function(y, xds_obj, s) {
  with(xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]$ix, {
    list(
      M = y[M_ix],
      Y = y[Y_ix]
    )
  })
}
```

`parse_MY_orbits.newMYname` extracts the same state variables from the solver
output matrix. It can also return derived quantities, such as prevalence or
parity, when those quantities are defined for the model.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Parse newMYname model output
#' @description Implements [ramp.xds::parse_MY_orbits] for newMYname.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::parse_MY_orbits
#' @return a named list
#' @export
parse_MY_orbits.newMYname <- function(outputs, xds_obj, s) {
  with(xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]$ix, {
    M <- outputs[, M_ix]
    Y <- outputs[, Y_ix]
    list(M = M, Y = Y)
  })
}
```

## Initial values

`make_MY_inits_newMYname` returns a named list containing an initial value for
every state variable. `setup_MY_inits.newMYname` stores those values in the
module object, and `change_MY_inits.newMYname` updates named values after
setup.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Make newMYname initial values
#' @param nPatches number of patches
#' @param options named values that override defaults
#' @param M initial adult mosquito density
#' @param Y initial infected mosquito density
#' @return a named list
#' @export
make_MY_inits_newMYname <- function(nPatches, options = list(), M = 10, Y = 1) {
  with(options, {
    M <- checkIt(M, nPatches)
    Y <- checkIt(Y, nPatches)
    list(M = M, Y = Y)
  })
}

#' @title Set up newMYname initial values
#' @description Implements [ramp.xds::setup_MY_inits] for newMYname.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::setup_MY_inits
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @export
setup_MY_inits.newMYname <- function(xds_obj, options = list(), s = 1) {
  xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]$inits <-
    make_MY_inits_newMYname(xds_obj$nPatches, options)
  xds_obj
}

#' @title Change newMYname initial values
#' @description Implements [ramp.xds::change_MY_inits] for newMYname.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::change_MY_inits
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @export
change_MY_inits.newMYname <- function(xds_obj, options = list(), s = 1) {
  xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]$inits[names(options)] <- options
  xds_obj
}
```

## Parameters and bionomics

Implement `get_MY_pars.newMYname` and `change_MY_pars.newMYname` for the
parameters users should inspect and change. For bionomic parameters managed
through shared ports, implement `MBionomics.newMYname` to evaluate their
baseline values at time `t`, and `MEffectSizes.newMYname` to apply the
intervention effects. These methods receive `t`, `y`, `xds_obj`, and `s`, and
return the updated `xds_obj`.

The SI module is an example of a module using the shared parameter helpers
for feeding rate (`f`), human fraction (`q`), mortality (`g`), emigration
(`sigma`), emigration loss (`mu`), egg-batch rate (`nu`), and EIP duration.
Use only the parameters relevant to the model.

## Dynamics

Implement one dynamics method for the model family: `dMYdt.newMYname` for a
continuous-time model, or `Update_MYt.newMYname` for a discrete-time model.
Both methods receive `t`, the dependent-variable vector `y`, `xds_obj`, and
the vector-species index `s`. Return values in the same order used for the
state indices.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Compute newMYname derivatives
#' @description Implements [ramp.xds::dMYdt] for newMYname.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::dMYdt
#' @return a numeric vector of derivatives
#' @export
dMYdt.newMYname <- function(t, y, xds_obj, s) {
  # Retrieve the shared terms needed by this model.
  Lambda <- xds_obj$terms$Lambda[[s]]
  kappa <- xds_obj$terms$kappa[[s]]

  with(get_MY_vars(y, xds_obj, s), {
    with(xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]], {
      # Replace these placeholders with the model's equations.
      dM <- ...
      dY <- ...
      c(dM, dY)
    })
  })
}
```

For discrete-time models, implement the update equations directly and return
the updated state vector; do not return derivatives or add them to the
current state unless that is the model's defined update rule.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Update newMYname states
#' @description Implements [ramp.xds::Update_MYt] for newMYname.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::Update_MYt
#' @return a numeric vector of updated states
#' @export
Update_MYt.newMYname <- function(t, y, xds_obj, s) {
  with(get_MY_vars(y, xds_obj, s), {
    with(xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]], {
      M_next <- ...
      Y_next <- ...
      c(M_next, Y_next)
    })
  })
}
```

## Interface outputs

Implement the following methods with one value per patch:

- `F_fqZ.newMYname` returns the daily density of infectious mosquito bites on
  humans (`fqZ`). The transmission interface uses it to compute EIR by human
  stratum.
- `F_fqM.newMYname` returns the daily density of mosquito bites on humans
  (`fqM`). The transmission interface uses it to compute HBR by human
  stratum.
- `F_eggs.newMYname` returns daily egg production by adult mosquitoes in each
  patch. The egg-laying interface distributes the eggs among habitats.

Each method receives `t`, `y`, `xds_obj`, and `s`.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Compute newMYname infective biting density
#' @description Implements [ramp.xds::F_fqZ] for newMYname.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::F_fqZ
#' @return a numeric vector with one value per patch
#' @export
F_fqZ.newMYname <- function(t, y, xds_obj, s) {
  with(get_MY_vars(y, xds_obj, s), {
    with(xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]], {
      fqZ <- ...
      fqZ
    })
  })
}

#' @title Compute newMYname human biting density
#' @description Implements [ramp.xds::F_fqM] for newMYname.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::F_fqM
#' @return a numeric vector with one value per patch
#' @export
F_fqM.newMYname <- function(t, y, xds_obj, s) {
  with(get_MY_vars(y, xds_obj, s), {
    with(xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]], {
      fqM <- ...
      fqM
    })
  })
}

#' @title Compute newMYname egg production
#' @description Implements [ramp.xds::F_eggs] for newMYname.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::F_eggs
#' @return a numeric vector with one value per patch
#' @export
F_eggs.newMYname <- function(t, y, xds_obj, s) {
  with(get_MY_vars(y, xds_obj, s), {
    with(xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]], {
      eggs <- ...
      eggs
    })
  })
}
```

## Skill set and checks

Implement `setup_skillset_MY.newMYname` to record the module's capabilities
and limitations. Implement `check_MY.newMYname` for model-specific setup
checks that should run before solving.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Set up newMYname skill set
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::setup_skillset_MY
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @export
setup_skillset_MY.newMYname <- function(xds_obj, s) {
  xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]$skill_set <- list()
  xds_obj
}

#' @title Check newMYname setup
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::check_MY
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @export
check_MY.newMYname <- function(xds_obj, s) {
  xds_obj
}
```

## Optional methods and tests

Implement `steady_state_M.newMYname`, `steady_state_Y.newMYname`, or
`steady_state_MY.newMYname` only when the corresponding steady state is
defined for the model. The MY interface does not define MY-specific plotting
generics; model-specific plots can use the parsed output from
`parse_MY_orbits.newMYname`.

Add the module to the appropriate source file in `ramp.library` and write
tests that check the equations and integration with `ramp.xds`. For example,
check that initial values have the expected names and dimensions, that
derivatives or updates preserve state ordering, and that the biting and egg
outputs have one value per patch.

## Reusable model code

**`ramp.xds`** has a modular design that allows published models to serve as
dynamical components in new models for malaria and other mosquito-transmitted
pathogens, including ordinary and delay differential equation models and
stochastic or deterministic discrete-time models.

The mathematics supporting this framework are described in [Spatial Dynamics
of Malaria Transmission](https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010684){target="_blank"}.
^[Wu SL, Henry JM, Citron DT, Mbabazi Ssebuliba D, Nakakawa Nsumba J, Sánchez C. HM, et al. (2023) Spatial dynamics of malaria transmission. PLoS Comput Biol 19(6): e1010684. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010684]
